key_insight: MLP-mixer neural wave functions offer competitive quantum-state representations, while a hierarchical mixer–transformer architecture outperforms compared state-of-the-art models on large quantum systems.
engineering_relevance: Lightweight information mixing offers a route to scalable classical simulation of quantum many-body systems without relying solely on costly self-attention.
method: Use an MLP mixer as a wave function ansatz to mix information globally and locally.
Benchmark against RNNs and transformers with single-site and patched inputs.
Combine the mixer and transformer in a hierarchical architecture.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ground-state benchmarks on two-dimensional quantum many-body systems across phases and sizes, evaluating representational accuracy and computational efficiency.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical accuracy, runtime, or memory results, so practical scaling gains require verification in the full paper.
paper_title: Scalable Neural Wave Functions via Information Mixing and Hierarchical Network Architectures
